source.title: Scalable MatMul-free Language Modeling
source.authors: Rui-Jie Zhu; Yu Zhang; Steven Abreu; Ethan Sifferman; Tyler Sheaves; Yi-Qiao Wang; Dustin Richmond; S. Shrestha; Peng Zhou; J. Eshraghian

record.tranche_reason: Applies loss-scaling analysis to a new language-model architecture, the MatMul-free LM, and reports downstream benchmark results at multiple model sizes.
record.gate_note: Figure 2 reports scaling-law loss projections for MatMul-free LM and Transformer++; plotted loss values are not transcribed numerically in the text, and the paper does not state that these are held-out losses. The benchmark table reports each model's zero-shot scores separately. Figure 4's training-loss curve and the failed-convergence comparison concern training dynamics, not a test of the stated scaling versions; those results are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.test_reason: The study fits scaling-law curves to its own 370M/1.3B/2.7B runs of a new MatMul-free ternary architecture and a Transformer++ baseline (Fig. 2). It also reports zero-shot scores at each size (Table 1). Both bear weakly on V1 and V6 in a new architectural setting. The loss fit is shown only as a figure, with no fitted parameters or fit quality.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report a steeper fitted scaling curve for MatMul-free LM than Transformer++, projected to intersect near 10^23 FLOPs, and suggest it could match or beat Transformer++ in loss at that scale. They also state that the downstream performance gap narrows with model size, 'consistent with the scaling law'.
record.recipe_differences: Tests scaling projections for a new MatMul-free recurrent/ternary-weight architecture rather than reproducing Kaplan or Hoffmann's scaling experiments; only three model sizes are used for the plotted scaling comparison.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports different learning dynamics for MatMul-free and conventional Transformer training, uses different learning rates and schedules for the two model types, and observes a late-stage S-shaped training-loss decrease for the MatMul-free model.

fits_no_version.finding: The fitted loss-vs-compute curve for the ternary MatMul-free LM is steeper than Transformer++'s, and the authors project a crossover near 10^23 FLOPs. This rests on three sizes per family, with different learning rates and schedules for each family.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling exponents of loss versus compute differ across architecture families (e.g. ternary recurrent vs full-precision Transformer).

fits_no_version.finding: The 370M MatMul-free LM shows an S-shaped late drop in training loss as the learning rate approaches 0. A MatMul-free Transformer++ with ternarized attention fails to converge.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training schedules and attention/architecture choices can substantially affect training-loss dynamics and convergence in ternary MatMul-free language models.

record.problems: The scaling comparison uses only three model sizes, reports projections rather than a validation of forecasts on much larger runs, and does not state whether Figure 2's loss is held-out. The downstream comparison changes training-token count between 370M and larger models, and the text does not report uncertainty for benchmark scores.

untested.parts: Fitted exponents and goodness of fit; held-out loss; separate parameter and token sweeps; range beyond three model sizes.
The projected crossover near 10^23 FLOPs is an untested extrapolation. No larger run checks it.
No fitted predictive relation between downstream scores and scale or loss. Only three sizes are reported, and the 370M runs use 15B tokens versus 100B for the larger runs.

record.verdict_notes: V1 gets no verdict: Fig. 2 gives no fitted parameters, fit quality or held-out status, and is based on three points per family. The scaling fit is mainly used as a tool to project a crossover, which is an untested extrapolation. Rows R03–R20 (370M) are baseline points for V6, so cannot_determine is appropriate for them. Downstream gains from 370M to 1.3B confound parameters with tokens (15B vs 100B), but compute rises either way. No uncertainty is reported for any score.

versions.untested_parts: The paper reports a loss-versus-compute scaling projection, but does not identify the plotted loss as held-out. It does not separately sweep parameters or tokens while holding the other quantities non-bottlenecking.
No comparison of predictions fitted on small runs against observed losses of runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute search for a loss-minimising parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
No other modality or training regime is tested.
Reports zero-shot task scores at several sizes, but does not fit a predictive relationship between downstream scores and scale or pretraining loss.
Does not compare fitted scaling exponents or compute-optimal allocations across counting, schedule, data, or fitting choices.

rows.subject: MatMul-free LM scaling-law projection
rows.operation_detail: Fits and plots a scaling-law loss curve against training compute using the reported model sizes.

conditions.value: Figure axis spans approximately 10^16 to 10^24 FLOPs

rows.note: The paper calls this a scaling-law projection and describes its descent as steeper than Transformer++; held-out status is not stated. The plotted series covers three model sizes.
rows.check: Figure only, with three points per family. No fitted exponent, residuals or held-out status are given, so a power-law fit 'over several orders of magnitude' cannot be read. 'Partial' is not supported by any stated number.

relationships.condition: Transformer++, MatMul-free RWKV-4 and MatMul-free LM, 370M to 1.3B to 2.7B, on ARCe, HS, OQ, PQ and most other cells
relationships.reason: Zero-shot accuracy rises with model size and compute in Table 1, e.g. HS 34.3→49.3→54.2 for Transformer++. Rows R21–R31, R33–R39, R41–R49.
relationships.display_finding: Zero-shot accuracy generally rises with model size and compute, with Transformer++ HellaSwag scores increasing from 34.3 to 49.3 to 54.2.

relationships.condition: Near-chance benchmarks (WinoGrande, ARC-Challenge) at some size steps
relationships.reason: Gains are negligible or slightly negative: RWKV-4 WGe +0.2 (R32), Transformer++ ARCc +0.3 (R40), MatMul-free LM WGe -0.3 (R50).
relationships.display_finding: WinoGrande changed by +0.2 for RWKV-4 and −0.3 for MatMul-free LM, while Transformer++ gained only +0.3 on ARC-Challenge.
